findings.source_passage: However, nothing dispirits, and nothing seems worth while disputing. He bolts down all events
findings.source_locator: paragraph 1, between the joke-at-his-expense clause and the ostrich simile
findings.why_it_matters: The transitional sentence 'nothing dispirits, and nothing seems worth while disputing' is a rhythmically and rhetorically distinct beat that sets up the 'bolts down' metaphor; its omission makes the opening paragraph feel abrupt and loses a key voice marker.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'However, nothing dispirits, and nothing seems worth while disputing' before 'He bolts down all events' to preserve the rhetorical rhythm of the opening philosophical paragraph.

findings.source_passage: It may seem strange that of all men sailors should be tinkering at their last wills and testaments, but there are no people in the world more fond of that diversion. This was the fourth time in my nautical life that I had done the same thing.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after the will-making decision, before 'After the ceremony was concluded'
findings.why_it_matters: This digressive observation is a classic Ishmael aside—ironic, generalizing, voice-establishing—and the detail that this is the fourth time is an interpretively significant autobiographical anchor; both are entirely missing from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two sentences beginning 'It may seem strange that of all men sailors…' and 'This was the fourth time in my nautical life…' before 'After the ceremony was concluded.'

findings.source_passage: Flask. "Can't you twist that smaller?" said Flask.
findings.why_it_matters: Flask's verbatim phrasing—'Can't you twist that smaller?', 'squint for squint'—is character-defining comic voice; the draft reduces it to a paraphrase that strips the humor and idiosyncrasy entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Flask's full verbatim dialogue including 'Can't you twist that smaller?' and 'squint for squint, mind that!' to preserve the comic register.

findings.source_passage: Here then, from three impartial witnesses, I had a deliberate statement of the entire case.
findings.why_it_matters: This mock-legal framing sentence establishes the satirical register of the entire 'considering…considering…' anaphoric passage that follows; its loss slightly flattens the ironic legal-brief parody.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Here then, from three impartial witnesses, I had a deliberate statement of the entire case' as the opening to the chain-of-considerations paragraph.

summary: The draft preserves the opening philosophy and closing paragraphs well but erases two medium-weight voice passages (the sailors-and-wills digression and the lead-in 'nothing dispirits' sentence) and flattens Flask's distinctively comic dialogue, together constituting three medium-severity findings that trigger regeneration.
